record.paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
record.original_question: Let λ_k and μ_k denote the Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacian eigenvalues of a bounded planar domain Ω of area A, with μ₀ = 0. Do Pólya’s conjectures hold, namely μ_k < 4πk/A < λ_k for every k = 1, 2, ...? More generally, are Dirichlet eigenvalues always above, and Neumann eigenvalues always below, their Weyl asymptotic values in all dimensions?

evidence.quote: Perhaps the most compelling of these are Pólya's conjectures for the Dirichlet and Neumann eigenvalues of the Laplacian ... For n = 2, these statements are expressed concisely by μ_k < 4πk/A < λ_k for k = 1,2,....

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded planar domain of area $A$. Denote by 
$$0 < \lambda_1 \le \lambda_2 \le \lambda_3 \le \cdots$$
the eigenvalues of the Dirichlet Laplacian on $\Omega$ (i.e., $-\Delta u = \lambda u$ in $\Omega$, $u = 0$ on $\partial\Omega$), and by
$$0 = \mu_0 \le \mu_1 \le \mu_2 \le \cdots$$
the eigenvalues of the Neumann Laplacian on $\Omega$ (with vanishing normal derivative on $\partial\Omega$).

(a) Prove or disprove Pólya's conjectures: for every $k = 1, 2, 3, \ldots$,
$$\mu_k \;<\; \frac{4\pi k}{A} \;<\; \lambda_k.$$

(b) More generally, for a bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ ($n \ge 2$) of volume $V$, let $\lambda_k$ and $\mu_k$ denote the corresponding Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacian eigenvalues. Let
$$W_k \;=\; \frac{(2\pi)^2 \, k^{2/n}}{(\omega_n V)^{2/n}},$$
where $\omega_n$ is the volume of the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^n$, denote the leading Weyl asymptotic value. Is it true that
$$\mu_k \;<\; W_k \;<\; \lambda_k \qquad \text{for all } k \ge 1?$$
artifact.status_search_result: Pólya's conjectures are known for tiling domains (Pólya, 1961). Filonov, Levitin, Polterovich, and Sobolev (Inventiones, 2023; arXiv:2203.07696) proved the Dirichlet form of Pólya's conjecture for Euclidean balls in all dimensions and for planar disks and sectors; extensions to annuli appeared in 2025/2026 (arXiv:2505.21737), and to cylinders in 2025 (arXiv:2511.17050). The conjectures remain open for general bounded domains in any dimension.

status_evidence.title: Pólya's conjecture for Euclidean balls
status_evidence.snippet: We prove Pólya's eigenvalue conjecture for the Dirichlet Laplacian on Euclidean balls in arbitrary dimension, as well as for planar disks and sectors.
status_evidence.claim: Pólya's conjecture proved for Dirichlet Laplacian on balls, disks, sectors.

status_evidence.title: Pólya's conjecture for Dirichlet eigenvalues of annuli
status_evidence.snippet: We prove Pólya's conjecture for the Dirichlet Laplacian on planar annuli.
status_evidence.claim: Extension to annular domains established in 2025/2026.

status_evidence.title: Mathematicians prove Pólya's conjecture for the eigenvalues of a disk
status_evidence.snippet: Filonov, Levitin, Polterovich and Sobolev resolved Pólya's conjecture for the disk, the first non-tiling case.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms partial resolution; full conjecture for arbitrary domains remains open.
